rebuttal_or_critique: I remain unconvinced by the arguments for continuing the 'withdrawal of accommodation' stance. With headline CPI at 4.25%, we are effectively at the target. Maintaining a stance of withdrawal of accommodation is inconsistent with a policy rate that is already providing a significantly positive real interest rate. The economy is showing robust GVA growth of 7.80%, and there is no evidence that the current policy rate is insufficient to keep inflation on a glide path to 4%. Persisting with a stance that signals a bias toward tightening when the data suggests we have reached a state of equilibrium risks unnecessary damage to the growth recovery. I must hold my ground on the necessity of a neutral stance to reflect the current macroeconomic reality.
